analysis.title: Gridlock and diplomatic hopes lift US stocks (UBS House View - Daily EMEA)
key_insights: The S&P 500 closed 1.6% higher on Wednesday and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.4%, reversing an initial negative futures reaction to the Democrats' win in both the House and the Senate.
The 10-year US Treasury yield fell 8bps from its pre-election level and the DXY dollar index was down 0.3%.
Risk sentiment was fragile early Thursday. AI-heavy indices in South Korea and Taiwan were down 5.4% and 3.2%, and Nasdaq futures priced a 1.2% decline at publication.
UBS says the election removed a source of uncertainty. A Democratic Congress with Trump keeping the presidency and veto should make abrupt tax and spending changes harder.
The S&P 500 gained an average of 15.5% in the six months after the previous 14 midterm elections since 1970. UBS says this is not a forecast.

Political risks remain: government funding, the debt ceiling (a possible source of bond volatility), and Democratic gains in data center states that could delay projects or raise costs. Trump keeps broad executive authority over tariffs, foreign policy and regulation.

Large technology platforms rose on Wednesday while data-center construction names fell on concern about scrutiny of electricity use, water use and permitting in states such as Texas and Georgia. UBS expects more dispersion within technology.
Investors favor platforms that fund investment from existing cash flow over businesses exposed to financing, construction, permitting or execution risk.

Brent crude fell 8.2% overnight to around USD 93.8/bbl on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy, with Qatar stepping up mediation. Iranian officials say a deal is only possible if the US accepts Iran's seven points.

UBS sees oil support from sharply lower global inventories, largely completed strategic reserve releases, record freight costs, constrained tanker capacity and recovering Chinese imports. Renewed military action remains a risk.

Eurozone October headline inflation rose to 4.0% y/y from 3.8%, a three-year high. Core held at 2.5% and services rose to 3.3% from 3.2%. This reinforced expectations for an ECB rate hike in December.
The euro rose 0.3% to around 1.12 and the dollar index slipped toward 101. UBS expects the dollar to stay weak and EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end.

Chinese AI and cloud developers reportedly ordered about 6 million NVIDIA RTX Pro 5500 chips, worth roughly USD 70bn, per Bloomberg. Buyers expect to receive only about 1% of the order over the next four months.
UBS forecasts aggregate AI capital spending of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028, while noting investors are weighing overinvestment, financing and monetization risks.

sector_views.rationale: Named among UBS's preferred sectors, supported by strong earnings and resilient growth.
UBS advises rebalancing concentrated exposure and favors cash-flow-funded platforms and high-quality infrastructure providers over businesses reliant on external funding.

earnings_insights: UBS says recent corporate results show robust demand across parts of the technology sector and the broader economy, with accelerating cloud revenue and expanding advance orders for computing capacity. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Three-year high, up from 3.8% in September. Supports expectations for an ECB hike in December.
UBS expects a recovery from about 1.12 on a weaker dollar.
UBS forecast, rising to USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028.

trade_ideas.description: Maintain diversified commodity exposure across energy, precious metals, industrial metals and agriculture as protection against geopolitical disruption
trade_ideas.rationale: Broad commodity exposure can help diversify portfolios when geopolitical disruption weighs on both stocks and bonds.
trade_ideas.risk: Diplomatic progress could put further downward pressure on oil prices.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce excess US dollar exposure progressively, shifting dollar cash or fixed income into high-quality bonds in required currencies or selectively hedging currency exposure on US assets
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS expects the dollar to stay weak, with EURUSD recovering toward 1.16 by year-end.
trade_ideas.risk: Energy prices, European sovereign spreads and geopolitical developments could make the path volatile.

trade_ideas.description: Rebalance concentrated technology exposure toward financially strong platforms and high-quality AI infrastructure providers
trade_ideas.rationale: Greater data center scrutiny and AI monetization questions could increase single-stock volatility.

risk_factors: US-Iran talks could break down or renewed attacks could occur, pushing oil higher.
Oil inventories have fallen sharply and strategic reserve releases are largely complete, so continued undersupply could support prices.
Government funding and debt ceiling negotiations could raise bond market volatility.
Democratic gains in data center states could delay projects, raise development costs or change where capacity is built.
Investors are weighing AI overinvestment, financing and monetization risks.
Crowded speculative dollar positioning could amplify a dollar decline.
Trump retains broad executive authority over tariffs, foreign policy and regulation.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures priced a 1.2% decline early Thursday, and AI-heavy indices in South Korea and Taiwan fell 5.4% and 3.2%.
UBS says speculative positioning in favor of the dollar is crowded and could amplify any dollar decline.
The US debt ceiling and government funding fights could increase bond market volatility.
geopolitical: Qatar is stepping up mediation as Washington and Tehran signal a possible return to talks on ending the US-Iran conflict.
Iranian officials say an agreement is only possible if the US accepts Iran's seven points.
Trump said no military strike is imminent. An open question is how long the US will support energy flows with military escorts.
Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the US midterm elections, while Trump keeps the presidency and veto power.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings are supportive, with accelerating cloud revenue, expanding advance orders for computing capacity and large Chinese chip orders. UBS forecasts AI capex rising to USD 1.5tr by 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic gains in data center states could delay projects and raise costs, and investors are weighing overinvestment, financing and monetization risks. AI-heavy Asian indices fell 5.4% and 3.2% and Nasdaq futures priced a 1.2% decline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Greater scrutiny of electricity consumption, water use and permitting in data center states such as Texas and Georgia, or a further drop in AI-heavy indices, would weaken the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Both sides have incentives to avoid a prolonged conflict, and Trump said no military strike is imminent. Brent fell 8.2% to around USD 93.8/bbl.
tension_points.bear_case: Global inventories have fallen sharply, strategic reserve releases are largely complete, and freight costs and tanker constraints are record. Iran says a deal needs the US to accept its seven points.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed military action or a breakdown in US-Iran negotiations would trigger another rise in oil prices.
